- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Louvre Museum has adapted its approach to exhibiting art in several ways: inclusivity, interpretation, collaboration, re-evaluation, and digitization.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The museum has become more inclusive, emphasizing non-Western art and representation of female and minority artists.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The museum provides more extensive interpretation and contextualization of art, including detailed labels, audio guides, and multimedia displays.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Louvre has collaborated with other institutions for interactive exhibitions, including joint exhibitions with the Met in New York and the British Museum in London.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The museum has re-evaluated its collection to remove or contextualize culturally insensitive or offensive art, providing background information on items related to colonialism and imperialism.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Louvre has increasingly used digital technologies for accessibility, including online exhibitions, virtual tours, and mobile apps.
